messages.content:
Three independent readers read the same non-disclosure agreement (NDA) and decided whether it supports one statement (the hypothesis). They may agree or disagree, and a program has checked each of their quotes against the document. Your job is to make the final decision yourself, from the document.

<document>
<document 165 omitted, sha256 3c1ab3de6177de46>
</document>

<hypothesis>
Confidential Information shall only include technical information.
</hypothesis>

<readings>
<reading id="A">
label: Contradiction
confidence: 95
reason: The definition of Confidential Information expressly covers non-technical items such as customer lists, marketing materials, finances, and product plans, and it may also include third-party information, so it is not limited to technical information.
<quote check="exact">including without limitation documents, prototypes, samples, plant and equipment, research, product plans, products, services, customer lists, software, developments, inventions, processes, designs, drawings, engineering, hardware configuration, marketing materials or finances</quote>
<quote check="exact">Confidential Information may also include information disclosed to a disclosing party by third parties.</quote>
</reading>
<reading id="B">
label: Contradiction
confidence: 92
reason: The agreement defines Confidential Information broadly to cover business information such as customer lists, marketing materials and finances, not only technical information.
<quote check="exact">certain confidential technical and business information</quote>
<quote check="exact">customer lists, software, developments, inventions, processes, designs, drawings, engineering, hardware configuration, marketing materials or finances</quote>
</reading>
<reading id="C">
label: Contradiction
confidence: 93
reason: The definition expressly covers business information such as customer lists, marketing materials and finances, not only technical information.
<quote check="exact">certain confidential technical and business information</quote>
<quote check="exact">customer lists, software, developments, inventions, processes, designs, drawings, engineering, hardware configuration, marketing materials or finances</quote>
</reading>
</readings>

The readings are evidence about where to look, not votes: a majority can be wrong, and a quote marked "missing" was not found in the document. Read the relevant parts of the document yourself.

Choose exactly one label:
- Entailment: the document states or clearly implies that the hypothesis is true.
- Contradiction: the document states or clearly implies that the hypothesis is false.
- NotMentioned: the document does not address the hypothesis, or says too little to decide.

Evidence is required. For Entailment or Contradiction, give 1 to 3 quotes copied character for character from the document (no paraphrase, no ellipses), each as short as it can be while still carrying the point. They will be checked against the document. For NotMentioned, give an empty list.

Give a confidence from 0 to 100: your probability, in percent, that your label is correct. Give a one-sentence reason.

Answer only with the JSON object the response format asks for: label, confidence, quotes, reason.

content.text: {"label": "Contradiction", "confidence": 95, "quotes": ["certain confidential technical and business information", "customer lists", "marketing materials or finances"], "reason": "The agreement defines Confidential Information to include business information such as customer lists, marketing materials and finances, so it is not limited to technical information."}
